correctness.rationale: The proof is an exact harmonic decomposition. The order-three projection condition permits precisely circle frequencies \(0\), \(\pm1\), and multiples of three. The source's harmonic-projection lemma isolates every spherical-harmonic degree, and its great-circle frequency lemma forces forbidden frequency \(2\) for each nonzero even degree at least two and forbidden frequency \(5\) for each nonzero odd degree at least five. Degrees zero, one, and three are exactly sufficient. The standard support-function condition \(\nabla^2_{S^2}h+hI\succeq0\), plus antipodal oddness of degree three, gives the operator-norm inequality and constant-width conclusion. No finite experiment is used as proof.
risks: The argument depends on the full quantifiers of the cited harmonic-projection and great-circle frequency lemmas; those portions of the preprint were inspected directly.
No claim is made about higher-dimensional analogues.

value.rationale: The source identifies order three as the sole exceptional rotational order in dimension three but gives examples rather than the full exceptional class. The classification is a natural completion: it shows all exceptions, not merely perturbative ones, are constant-width bodies whose translated support functions are precisely admissible degree-three harmonics. The resulting seven-dimensional compact convex parameter body is a structural description with clear future use for extremal questions inside the exceptional family.
risks: The parameter body is not further classified up to rotations, so congruence classes are not enumerated.
The result is dimension-specific and does not settle the source's higher-dimensional extension.
